title: MIL-DTL-38999 contact size vs. current capacity and wire gauge
description: Per-contact current-carrying capacity and accommodated wire gauge (AWG) for the standard MIL-DTL-38999 / MIL-STD-1560 contact sizes. Used to filter insert arrangements in the connector builder by the current load they can carry on a single contact.
current_basis: Maximum continuous test current per contact at sea level, mated, Service Rating M, taken from MIL-DTL-38999 manufacturer catalog electrical-data tables. Real-world derating (bundle, altitude, ambient) reduces these values; treat as a per-contact ceiling, not a circuit guarantee.
rules: Larger contact size number = smaller physical size. Size 22D is the smallest/lowest-current; size 8 is the largest/highest-current.
Each contact size accepts a band of wire gauges; pick a wire AWG inside the contact's range so the crimp is rated.
A connector's current capacity is set by its contact sizes, not its shell size. To carry N amps on a circuit you need a contact rated >= N amps.
Coax and twinax size-8 / size-12 contacts are RF/data contacts and have no continuous power-current rating; do not use them for power loads.
Service rating and altitude derate the values below; size up a contact for high-altitude, high-bundle-density, or continuous-duty loads.
